title: WhatsApp Appointment Booking with Calendly and AI
summary: Build a WhatsApp appointment booking assistant that answers service questions, checks live Calendly times and creates the chosen appointment. Copy the full setup.
body_markdown:
Build a **WhatsApp appointment booking assistant** that answers a bicycle-repair question, offers live times and creates a **confirmed appointment in Calendly** . The customer asks about the service, chooses a time and supplies their details in the same WhatsApp conversation.


The example is **Harbor Cycle Workshop** , a fictional business offering a free **15-minute Repair assessment** . In our controlled WhatsApp test, the customer selected 10:00 on 27 October 2026 in Europe/London. The delivered confirmation matched the appointment in Calendly, from 10:00 to 10:15.


1. Choose an available time and send your details.


2. Receive the booking confirmation in the same chat.


*Real mobile WhatsApp screenshots. The confirmation matched the independently checked Calendly appointment. Emails and personal link details are hidden; contact labels are standardized to the workshop name.*


## What will the WhatsApp booking assistant do?


The customer completes three steps in WhatsApp:


Customer step What the Agent does


Ask about a puncture repair Explain the £12 starting labour price, additional parts cost and free assessment


Ask for an assessment date Read Calendly availability and offer times in the workshop’s time zone


Choose an offered time and give their name and email Create the requested appointment in Calendly, then return its confirmation and management links


You will build this in six steps: add the workshop knowledge, prepare the Calendly event, connect its tools, set the booking instructions, test the complete conversation and repeat it on WhatsApp. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is the connection that lets the Agent use Calendly’s availability and booking tools.


### What you need


1. [Create a Quickchat AI account](https://app.quickchat.ai/register) and verify your email if prompted. Business deployment needs a commercial plan and AI credits; Preview replies and Simulation Testing also use credits. Check[Quickchat AI pricing](https://quickchat.ai/pricing) .
2. Use Calendly **Standard or above** . Its[Booking API reference](https://developer.calendly.com/api-docs/calendly-api/scheduled-events/create-event-invitee) requires a paid plan to create appointments, even if the[MCP connection itself is free](https://calendly.com/help/connect-calendly-to-your-ai-tools) .
3. Have access to the intended Meta business account and WhatsApp Business Platform number. Follow the supported verification flow and check[Meta’s messaging rates](https://whatsappbusiness.com/products/platform-pricing/) .
4. Prepare a controlled customer phone and test inbox. Label and cancel test appointments. Replace the fictional business details before deployment.


[Download the Harbor Cycle Workshop kit](https://quickchat.ai/blog-assets/downloads/harbor-cycle-workshop-kit.zip) for the exact Main Prompt, five source articles, Calendly setup, handoff text and test inputs. These are editable setup files, not a one-click import. TheMain Prompt andknowledge sources also appear at the end of this guide.


Build and test in **AI Preview** first, then repeat the conversation on WhatsApp. To delegate part of the setup, use the optionalChatGPT or Claude walkthrough with the same kit.


## Step 1: Give the Agent its workshop knowledge


Five short articles give the Agent its service facts while keeping prices, opening hours and bookable times distinct.


*Use workshop knowledge for stable facts and Calendly for live times.*


1. In account setup, choose the description route. Enter “A service assistant for Harbor Cycle Workshop that answers bicycle-repair questions and books a 15-minute Repair assessment”, then select **Create my AI Agent** .
2. Continue with **Next** . Choose a plan or **Skip for now** to finish configuration. Open **Identity** and set the name to **Harbor Cycle Workshop** .
3. Open **Knowledge Base > Add Article** . Enter the first source’s title in **Create custom article** , then select **Create article** .
4. Paste the complete source into **Content** in **Edit Article** , select **Save** , and wait for **Ready** . Repeat for the other four sources. Each save processes its article.


*Paste the complete source into **Content** , then save it and check processing. The local editor shows the opening of the Services article.*


Source to copy What it establishes


1. Services The free 15-minute assessment is an inspection, not reserved repair work


2. Indicative prices Starting labour prices and additional parts costs


3. Hours and appointments Opening hours, appointment schedule and live availability are distinct


4. Location and contact In-person location and the route to staff


5. Human help and booking limits Confirmation, uncertain results, management links and fallback


The complete blocks are in thecopyable knowledge appendix and the kit’s` knowledge/` folder.


Leave stock, final quotes and completion dates to staff when adapting[your own approved documentation](https://quickchat.ai/post/create-ai-support-agent-from-documentation) .


**Check the first result:** once all five sources are Ready, ask “My bike has a puncture. How much might it cost, and what does the assessment cover?” in **AI Preview** . Look for the £12 starting labour price, parts charged separately, and an assessment that does not reserve repair work.


The same service check on WhatsApp: labour starts at £12, parts cost extra and the free assessment does not reserve repair work.


## Step 2: Prepare the Calendly appointment


Create one **Repair assessment** event with a fixed duration, location and schedule. The Agent will use this event’s identifier for availability and booking.


Calendly setting Demonstration value


Event name and type Repair assessment; one host and one customer


Duration 15 minutes


Location 14 Workshop Lane, Bristol, United Kingdom, explicitly fictional


Availability time zone Europe/London


Tuesday to Friday 10:00 to 16:00


Saturday 10:00 to 13:00


Monday and Sunday Unavailable


Payment and extra required questions None


1. In Calendly **Scheduling** , edit the intended event or select **+ Create** for a new one-on-one event. Fill **Event name** , **Duration** , **Location** and **Availability** , then select **Save changes** . Calendly’s[event-setup instructions](https://calendly.com/help/how-to-set-up-an-event-type) explain the controls.
2. Connect the calendar that Calendly should check for conflicts. Set the event’s own availability zone and hours, then add real holiday exceptions and booking limits. Avoid changing a shared schedule used by unrelated events.
3. In **More options > Notifications and automations** , edit the basic email or calendar-invitation notification. Enable **Include cancel and reschedule links in email invitations and reminders** , then save. These[personal management links](https://calendly.com/help/how-to-include-cancel-and-reschedule-links-for-invitees) give customers another route to manage their appointment.
4. Open the event’s public page and check its name, 15-minute duration, address and available dates. In **Scheduling** , use **Copy link** for this specific event and keep it as the fallback URL for Step 4.


*Check the assessment’s name, duration and location on its public scheduling page. This is the real demonstration event.*


The workshop opens at 09:00, but assessments start at 10:00. Calendly’s event schedule and connected calendar determine which appointments the Agent can offer.


## Step 3: Connect Calendly and limit its tools


The Calendly MCP connection gives the Agent named operations. Enable the reads needed to find the event and its times, then add booking only when the instructions and checks are ready.


*Concept: WhatsApp carries the conversation; Quickchat AI answers service questions and uses Calendly to find times and create the appointment.*


### Connect and set the tool list


1. Open **Actions & MCPs > Add Action > MCP** , choose **Calendly** in the catalog and complete its authorization flow with the controlled account.


*Choose **Connect with Calendly** to authorize the account. Real local setup screen.*


1. Open the resulting Action with **Edit Action** . Set **MCP action name** to **Harbor Cycle Workshop appointments** .
2. Under **Tools** , set **Default tool activation** to **Off** , then apply the table below and **Save** . If you use **Use recommended** , review the resulting switches: its cancellation tool is outside this recipe.


Tool During setup During the booking test


` users-get_current_user` On On


` event_types-list_event_types` On On


` event_types-list_event_type_available_times` On On


` meetings-create_invitee` Off On, after Step 4 and the service tests


` meetings-cancel_event` and every other Calendly tool Off Off


**Default tool activation** Off Off


*Enable booking for Step 5; keep it off during initial setup. Cancellation and Default tool activation stay off. Local settings example.*


Tool switches select the available operations. The Main Prompt specifies the workshop’s event, required customer details and when to book.


### Copy the event identifier without guessing


Before replacing the prompt’s two operator values, start a new **AI Preview** conversation with only the three read tools enabled. This setup request asks for event details, without checking times or creating an appointment:


Copy the read-only event lookup request


```text
Find the active Repair assessment event lasting 15 minutes in my connected Calendly account. Look up the account owner first and copy the returned owner URI unchanged when listing their events. Follow pagination if needed. Return the exact name, duration, uri and scheduling_url in one plain-text code block. Copy both URLs in full. If there is not exactly one match, stop and explain. Do not create, change or cancel anything.
```


Hover the reply and select **Copy** . Match the name, duration and public link against the event from Step 2. Keep the complete` uri` and` scheduling_url` for the two prompt settings below. If the lookup is ambiguous or fails, resolve that before enabling booking.


Use` uri` for tool calls and` scheduling_url` for the fallback page. Copy both complete values from the reply, including` https://` .


### Save the booking references for later turns


Expand` meetings-create_invitee` , even while its switch is off, to reveal **Save to memory** . Confirm these rows and **Save** :


JSONPath expression Memory key


` $.resource.event`` calendly_event_uri`


` $.resource.cancel_url`` calendly_cancel_url`


` $.resource.reschedule_url`` calendly_reschedule_url`


*Each JSONPath selects a response field; its memory key makes that value available to later messages. Local settings example.*


After booking, “Can I change the time?” should return this appointment’s saved rescheduling link.Step 5 checks that exact value without another booking or an email lookup.


Use **Europe/London** for the workshop’s appointment times. Quickchat AI converts the local dates in code and returns labelled options. The Agent uses the customer’s selected option to book.


How the event and appointment fields are filled


With both availability and booking enabled, the[Calendly tools accept local dates and an explicit time zone](https://docs.quickchat.ai/ai-agent/actions/mcp-actions/#calendly-appointment-times) . Quickchat AI handles UTC conversion and checks the selected slot again before submitting it to Calendly. The tool names remain the same.


Value Where it comes from Where it goes


Approved event identifier The verified event lookup Availability` event_type` and booking` post_invitee_request.event_type`


Requested date range Midnight on the requested date to midnight on the next calendar date Availability` local_start_time` ,` local_end_time` and` timezone`


Offered local time Each option’s returned` display_time` Customer’s choice and the booking confirmation


Selected appointment The option’s` local_start_time` , including its offset, and` timezone` Booking` post_invitee_request.local_start_time` and` booking_timezone`


Customer details Customer’s name, email and confirmed zone` post_invitee_request.invitee`


Fixed physical location The event and workshop configuration` post_invitee_request.location`


A clear request for an offered time plus the required customer details is enough to proceed. If the request is tentative or unclear, the Agent asks for confirmation first. Quickchat AI matches the chosen instant against current availability and sends Calendly its original timestamp.


## Step 4: Set the booking instructions and staff route


The Main Prompt joins the service facts and calendar tools into one conversation: **check times, get a clear choice and the required details, book, then confirm the result** . “I’ll take 10:00” with the customer’s name and email can complete the request. A tentative choice or missing detail prompts a question before booking.


“I’ll take 10:00” plus the required details makes a clear booking request. The Agent can proceed without asking the customer to repeat their choice.


### Install the complete Main Prompt


Open **Identity > Main Prompt** and paste the completeMain Prompt , also supplied as` main-prompt.txt` in the kit. Replace` NOT CONFIGURED` only on these two setting lines:


Prompt setting Value to paste


**Approved Calendly event type URI** Complete` uri` from Step 3


**Approved Calendly booking link** Verified public` scheduling_url`


Leave the later guard sentence unchanged. Main Prompt saves automatically; wait for saving to finish and reopen it to check the stored text. The fictional location appears in the knowledge, event and booking instruction. Update all three together for a real workshop.


*Set the event URI and fallback booking link in Main Prompt, then check the saved values. Real local editor.*


### Configure Human Handoff


Open **Actions & MCPs > Human Handoff** , enable it and turn **AI summary** on. In **Handoff Rules** , use the plus control to add **Workshop handoff** , enable the rule and paste the following into **Description** :


Copy the Workshop handoff Description


```text
Offer Human Handoff when the customer asks for a person; needs a final quote, parts availability or repair completion date; describes unsafe brakes, crash or frame damage, or an e-bike battery problem; or encounters a booking failure, uncertain booking result or problem with an existing appointment. Do not diagnose the bicycle, invent availability or claim that a booking was made or changed.
```


Set **Question** to:


```text
Would you like me to pass this conversation to the workshop team?
```


Set **Confirmation** to:


```text
Your conversation has been flagged for the workshop team to review. A member of staff can reply here when available. This handoff has not booked an appointment.
```


*The Question asks before handing off; Confirmation explains that staff can reply and no appointment was booked. Local settings example.*


Keep the explicit-user-request behaviour and **Lack of knowledge** enabled. Leave **Human Agents’ availability** unrestricted so customers can enter the queue while staff are offline. Use **Email notifications** only with a real monitored address; the fictional` .example` address cannot receive them. Save the settings.


Test this staff route after the booking conversation in Step 6.


## Step 5: Test the conversation and the calendar result


Run the four service questions first, then complete one booking conversation in **AI Preview** . Check the appointment in Calendly before moving the conversation to WhatsApp.


### Check service answers in Simulation Testing


Keep` meetings-create_invitee` off while checking the four service questions.


*Open **Testing** to create or find the workshop dataset. Local configuration example.*


1. Open **Testing** in the sidebar. The page title is **Simulation Testing** .
2. Choose **Create Dataset > Paste messages** and name it **Workshop service checks** .
3. Paste these four messages, separated by a line containing only` ---` , then select **Create** :


Copy the four service test messages


```text
My bike has a puncture. How much might it cost, and what does the assessment cover?
---
Are you open on Monday? Can I bring my bike on Saturday?
---
Do you have my inner tube in stock, and can you finish the repair tomorrow?
---
What should I bring to my Repair assessment?
```


Open the dataset, paste the following into **Evaluation criteria** , then **Save** :


Copy the service evaluation criteria


```text
Check service facts against the workshop knowledge. Puncture labour starts at £12 with parts extra. The free Repair assessment is 15 minutes and is not a repair reservation. Monday is closed. Saturday opening hours are 09:00 to 14:00 Europe/London, not evidence of available appointments. Do not promise stock, final prices, repair completion dates or that an unsafe bicycle is safe. Score the visible reply only; inspect Action calls and Calendly separately to verify bookings.
```


*The four service questions in the local dataset, ready for its first run.*


To run and review the checks:


1. Select **Run** , give the run a label such as` workshop service baseline` , review the displayed credit cost and select **Start Run** .
2. Open the completed run and read every reply, **AI Score** and evaluation justification. Use **View** to inspect its conversation.
3. Check any handoff assignment and summary in **Inbox** .


Each dataset item starts a fresh conversation. Use the continuous Preview test below for booking. The[support-agent testing guide](https://quickchat.ai/post/how-to-test-an-ai-support-agent) explains how to compare runs after an edit.


### Run one complete booking conversation


*Read availability, establish the requested appointment and collect its details. Confirm the booking only after Calendly returns success.*


After completing Steps 1–4 and the service checks, turn` meetings-create_invitee` on in **Tools** , **Save** , and start a new **AI Preview** conversation. Use a future date within the event’s booking range and an inbox you control.


Send in order Expected result


“My rear tyre has a puncture. What does a repair cost?” Starting labour price, parts extra and no binding quote


“I’d like a Repair assessment on \[full future date\], in Europe/London.” Available times on the requested date, labelled in the workshop’s time zone


“I’ll take option \[number\]. My name is \[test name\], my email is \[controlled email\].” One appointment matching the selected date and time, followed by its confirmation


“Can you send me the link to change the time?” The saved rescheduling URL, without a new booking


“What should I bring?” Preparation advice from the workshop knowledge


Replace the bracketed instructions with your test values. Keep the full date and time zone explicit. If a detail is missing or the request is unclear, answer the Agent’s question before continuing; it should not invent a name, email or appointment choice.


### Check the appointment and follow-up


1. In the matching **Inbox** conversation, expand the action-call indicator. Check that the booking call follows a clear choice and the customer’s required details.
2. Open the appointment in Calendly. Match its event, full date, time zone, duration, location and test customer with the requested appointment and delivered confirmation.
3. Ask for the rescheduling link and preparation advice. Compare the link with **Inbox > Details > Memory** , as shown in the inspection guide below.


*Expand the called Action to inspect its inputs and result. Local fixture with a synthetic booking response.*


*Compare the selected date, time and zone with the provider record, then clean up the controlled test.*


Inspect the Action log and saved booking links


For the Action’s history, open **Actions & MCPs** and select **View logs** on **Harbor Cycle Workshop appointments** . Open the booking call and inspect **Parameters sent** for the event identifier,` post_invitee_request.local_start_time` and` booking_timezone` where they are visible. Match the call to its conversation before comparing it with the customer’s choice and details.


*Choose **View logs** on the Action card to find its recorded calls. Local fixture.*


*Match the visible **Parameters sent** with the selected appointment. Local fixture with a synthetic booking request.*


Open the appointment in Calendly for its full details and match them with the customer’s requested appointment. This table maps those details to their booking fields:


Requested detail Booking request Saved appointment


Repair assessment, 15 minutes Approved` event_type` Correct event and duration


Full date, time and zone Selected` local_start_time` and` booking_timezone` ; invitee’s` timezone` separately The same instant, allowing for the operator’s display zone


Name and email` invitee` The intended test customer


Workshop address Physical` location` The same in-person location


For “Can you send me the link to change the time?”, open **Inbox > Details > Memory** . Hover **Calendly Reschedule Url** , select **Copy** , and compare the complete value with the reply’s destination.


*Open **Memory** and use **Copy** for the complete saved link. Local fixture with nonfunctional example URLs.*


This checks retrieval of this conversation’s link. It does not establish that the customer completed a reschedule.


### Check the date and time zone


Use the full date, including the year, and **Europe/London** for this in-person appointment. London changes between British Summer Time and GMT, so the same clock time can correspond to different UTC times. Quickchat AI’s Calendly integration handles that conversion in code and books with the matching timestamp returned by Calendly.


*The same London clock time corresponds to different UTC times before and after the clock change.*


When reading the appointment in Calendly, account for its displayed time zone when comparing it with the customer’s chosen time. For a clock-change date, the availability query must cover the whole local day: its two midnight boundaries can be 23 or 25 hours apart. If an hour differs, correct the date or zone handling and repeat the check before another booking.


Check changes of date, unavailable times and other edge cases Control Passing result


Change the date after selecting a time Fresh availability and a clear choice of the new appointment before booking


Ask for 09:00 because the workshop is open No invented slot; uses the assessment’s actual availability


Withhold the email or say “10:00 might work” A question to establish the missing detail or clear intent; no booking yet


Send only “yes” without an established current appointment Clarification, not a new booking


Repeat “yes” or ask for a management link after a successful booking Acknowledge the existing appointment; no second booking


Request an unavailable date or an occupied time No offer for an absent slot and no claim that alternatives are held or reserved


Ask to look up someone else’s booking by email No lookup or disclosure


Describe crash damage or brakes that may be unsafe No remote safety assurance; advice not to ride and staff help


Use separate conversations where a handoff would end the test. Include a summer-time date and a winter-time date when they are available for testing.


Troubleshoot a test that does not complete Symptom What to inspect Next step


No times for a day that looks open Event activation, event schedule, conflict calendar and requested local date range and zone Check the actual event’s availability; workshop opening hours do not establish slots


A reply or appointment is one hour out Returned` display_time` , approved local date/zone, selected` local_start_time` ,` booking_timezone` and provider display zone Stop booking tests, identify the first mismatch and repeat the local-time check before another write


Calendly rejects a booking Actual error, booking entitlement and required event fields Correct the specific configuration or missing field; do not infer failure from the chat alone


The result is uncertain Call history and the actual Calendly appointment Have staff establish whether a booking exists before any retry or public-page submission


The rescheduling link is missing Booking response capture and **Details > Memory** in the same conversation Check the three memory paths; use the customer’s confirmation or staff if no link was captured


WhatsApp sends no reply Matching Inbox item, connection/delivery state, remaining credits and assignee Resolve delivery or credit problems; return assignment to **AI Agent** if a completed handoff still pauses replies


A staff reply cannot be sent Time of the latest customer message Check the 24-hour window described in Step 6 before sending an ordinary reply


The[action reliability guide](https://quickchat.ai/post/reliable-ai-agent-actions) explains how to trace a result to the relevant instruction, call and saved record. Repeat the affected case and an ordinary booking conversation after a change.


Cancel the labelled Preview test appointment after recording its result and verify the cancellation in Calendly.


## Step 6: Complete the booking inside WhatsApp


Connect the tested Agent to the business number, then complete the same service-to-booking conversation from a controlled customer phone.


*The real local setup panel shows the number choices before connection. Select the route that matches your number.*


1. Open **Channels > External Apps > WhatsApp** and select **Connect WhatsApp** . Complete Meta’s supported account and number setup. The[WhatsApp connection documentation](https://docs.quickchat.ai/channels/whatsapp/) covers the current verification options.
2. Confirm that the intended number is enabled for this Agent. Send a customer-initiated service question from the test phone and inspect both the delivered reply and its Inbox conversation.
3. In the channel setup, look for **AI reply delivered** . **Waiting for your first message** and **Waiting for the AI reply to be delivered** are intermediate states.
4. Continue in that same conversation with thebooking sequence from Step 5 . Establish the full date and zone, clearly choose a returned time and give the controlled name and email. Check the confirmation on the phone and the corresponding booking call in Inbox.
5. Open the appointment in Calendly. Match its event, date, time zone, instant, duration and invitee with the WhatsApp request and confirmation.


In our WhatsApp test, the customer asked for a Repair assessment on **27 October 2026 in London** . The Agent offered 10:00, 10:30 and 11:00:


The customer asks for a date in London. The reply offers three times and names Europe/London explicitly.


The customer then selected **10:00** and supplied the test name and email. The next reply confirmed the appointment and included Calendly’s management links:


The booking completes inside WhatsApp. The confirmation gives the appointment details and personal cancel and reschedule links; private values are hidden here.


An independent Calendly check found one matching **15-minute assessment** , with the same date, time and test customer. We cancelled it after verification and confirmed that no matching active appointment remained.


See the matching Calendly response


This excerpt comes from the real Calendly event read before cleanup. On 27 October 2026, Europe/London is on GMT, so` 10:00:00Z` is 10:00 in London.


```text
{
"resource"  : {
"name"  :   "Repair assessment"  ,
"status"  :   "active"  ,
"start_time"  :   "2026-10-27T10:00:00Z"  ,
"end_time"  :   "2026-10-27T10:15:00Z"
}
}
```


We separately matched the test customer and event, then cancelled the appointment. Private identifiers and management links are omitted.


Finish in the same WhatsApp thread by asking “What should I bring?” and requesting the saved rescheduling link. Keep **the delivered conversation and matching Calendly appointment** together as the result of the test. Check any configured email notification separately in the test inbox, then cancel the labelled appointment and verify its cancellation.


Check staff handoff and the return to the Agent


Test Human Handoff after the booking conversation because it pauses AI replies. A queued conversation waits for staff to join; configure a monitored queue and avoid promising a response time.


1. From the customer phone, ask to speak to a person.
2. Open the matching **Inbox** conversation and check its handoff assignment and AI summary. Select **Assign to me** .
3. Use **Send message** to send a customer-visible staff reply. Confirm that the same reply arrives on the phone and inspect its **Delivered** or **Read** status. An internal note is not a customer message.
4. Select **AI Agent** in the assignee dropdown. Ask the preparation question from the phone again and check that the Agent resumes answering.


WhatsApp permits ordinary replies within 24 hours of the customer’s latest message. A new customer message resets that window. After it closes, the operator must wait for another customer message or use an approved message template; the ordinary reply composer is disabled. See[Meta’s messaging policy](https://whatsappbusiness.com/policy/) and the[Inbox guide](https://docs.quickchat.ai/conversations/inbox/) .


*An **AI Note** gives staff the conversation context. Earlier local handoff example; inspect this view after your own test.*


Use the public booking page when chat booking cannot proceed


When chat booking cannot proceed and no booking request is unresolved, offer the approved event link. Explain that the customer chooses the time, enters their details and confirms on Calendly. They should check the page’s displayed time zone and final confirmation. The Agent receives no automatic proof of that separate website submission.


If a booking may already exist, have staff check before trying again or sending the customer to submit through the page. For later changes, use this conversation’s saved management link or the customer’s Calendly confirmation; keep the cancellation tool off.


Before using the setup with customers, replace the fictional business details, check calendar exceptions and confirm who monitors the staff queue. Rerun the service checks and complete conversation after changing the knowledge, prompt or tools.


The[general Calendly scheduling tutorial](https://quickchat.ai/post/ai-scheduling-assistant-calendly) covers the broader tool and memory workflow; this build adds workshop knowledge and verification on WhatsApp.


## WhatsApp appointment booking FAQ


### Can customers book a Calendly appointment inside WhatsApp?


Yes. Quickchat AI can offer live Calendly times, collect the customer’s name and email, and create the chosen appointment inside the WhatsApp conversation. The public booking page is a fallback if chat booking cannot proceed; opening that link does not reserve a time.


### Does the customer need a Calendly account?


No. The business connects its Calendly account to Quickchat AI. The customer chooses an offered time and supplies their name and email in the conversation.


### Can I use the standalone WhatsApp Business app?


This Agent uses WhatsApp Business Platform through Quickchat AI’s channel connection. The standalone Business app alone does not run it. Use the supported number and verification options shown during connection.


### Is WhatsApp appointment booking free?


Creating appointments through Calendly’s Booking API requires Standard or above, even though connecting to its MCP server can be free. A deployed business Agent also needs a commercial Quickchat AI plan and AI credits. Meta’s charges depend on the messaging route, category and recipient market.


### When is the appointment actually booked?


After the customer clearly requests an available appointment, supplies the required details and Calendly successfully accepts the booking request. An offered time or an email address alone does not create a booking. Match the confirmation with the actual Calendly appointment.


### How do customers cancel or reschedule?


The Agent can share the personal management link saved from a booking it created in this conversation. If that link is unavailable, the customer uses their Calendly confirmation or asks staff. This recipe keeps the cancellation tool off and does not look up appointments by a typed email address.


### Will this send WhatsApp appointment reminders?


This recipe handles customer-initiated conversations and appointment creation. Calendly’s confirmation is separate from a WhatsApp reminder. Scheduled WhatsApp reminders require a separately tested scheduler, recipient consent, templates where required and delivery setup.


## Can ChatGPT or Claude prepare this WhatsApp assistant?


**The Quickchat AI account connector can prepare much of the Agent’s configuration.** It can save the supplied instructions and articles, prepare the service dataset and create a restricted Calendly Action. You review the remaining settings and authorize the external accounts.


This is a separate connection from Calendly MCP. Your AI client uses the account connector to manage the Agent; the Agent later uses Calendly’s tools in customer conversations.


*Open **Manage your AI in** above the dashboard sidebar. This real local panel connects an AI client to account management; connect the customer-facing WhatsApp number in Step 6.*


1. Open[Quickchat AI in ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6a4656c688748191be4c5247fb0d5dfc) and choose **Install plugin** , or use the[Quickchat AI listing in the Claude Directory](https://claude.ai/directory/connectors/app-quickchat-ai) . Sign in to the account that will own this Agent.
2. Extract the workshop kit. Attach its text files and all five files in` knowledge/` , or paste their contents into the conversation.
3. Send the setup request below and review any approvals your AI client presents.


Copy the account setup request


```text
Use the Quickchat AI connector to prepare Harbor Cycle Workshop from the attached tutorial kit. Inspect your available tools and my Agents first. Use a dedicated empty Agent or create one if needed. Leave my other working Agents alone. Show me the selected Agent’s name and ID.


Save main-prompt.txt and the five knowledge articles verbatim. Keep the two NOT CONFIGURED operator values until I supply the verified event URI and public link. Use calendly-setup.md for the event, tool and memory configuration.


If no matching Calendly Action exists, create Harbor Cycle Workshop appointments for https://mcp.calendly.com with only users-get_current_user, event_types-list_event_types and event_types-list_event_type_available_times enabled. Keep booking, cancellation and all other tools off. If an Action already exists, inspect it and list any tool-switch or memory-capture changes I must make in the dashboard; do not recreate it.


Create Workshop service checks from simulation-messages.txt and simulation-rubric.txt, without running it.
```
